deviation: No Flow | Air inlet to cathode
causes: Air compressor trip or LCV-200 fails closed (actuator/signal fault from IIC-400)
consequences: No O2/CO2 to cathode; cell voltage collapses and cells reverse; Ni anode/cathode damage. Unreacted fuel leaves via the anode outlet, and propulsion power is lost.
safeguards: FIT-110/FI-110 air flow indication; PIT-110/PI-110 pressure indication; VZA-100 low cell voltage alarm; BPCS air flow control via IIC-400/LCV-200
recommendations: Provide low-low air flow (FIT-110) trip that isolates fuel via LCV-100/LCV-300 and initiates controlled stack shutdown, independent of BPCS

deviation: Less Flow | Air inlet to cathode
causes: Partial blockage of the air filter/line, LCV-200 throttled by a control fault, or compressor degradation
consequences: Cathode air is the main stack coolant, so the stack overheats with local hot spots above 700 °C. This causes electrolyte evaporation/loss, corrosion and wet-seal damage, shortens stack life and could lead to gas leakage.
safeguards: FIT-110/FI-110; TE-200/TE-210 with TT-410 stack temperature indication; TE-310/TI-310 cathode outlet temperature; BPCS stack temperature control
recommendations: Add low air flow alarm on FIT-110 and high stack temperature alarm on TT-410

deviation: More Flow | Air inlet to cathode
causes: LCV-200 fails open or IIC-400 control fault
consequences: Stack is over-cooled and large thermal gradients develop. If the temperature falls below about 490 °C the carbonate electrolyte freezes and the matrix cracks, leading to gas crossover and permanent stack damage.
safeguards: FIT-110/FI-110; TE-200/TE-210, TT-410; BPCS temperature and air flow control
recommendations: Add low stack temperature alarm and high air flow alarm with automatic air flow limitation

deviation: No Flow | Feed (natural gas + water) to reformer
causes: NG compressor or water pump trip, or LCV-100 fails closed
consequences: Anode is starved of H2/CO and the Ni anode oxidises, causing voltage collapse and loss of power. If H2 BOG continues, the endothermic reforming heat sink is lost and the stack overheats.
safeguards: FIT-100/FI-100; PIT-100/PI-100; VZA-100 low voltage alarm; TT-410 stack temperature
recommendations: Interlock low feed flow (FIT-100) to reduce DC load via IIC-400 and limit H2 BOG via LCV-300

deviation: More Flow | Feed (natural gas + water) to reformer
causes: LCV-100 fails open or flow control fault
consequences: Excess endothermic reforming cools the stack locally (risk of electrolyte freezing at the inlet). Excess unreacted CH4/H2 goes to the anode outlet and downstream, and fuel is wasted.
safeguards: FIT-100/FI-100; TE-200/TE-210, TT-410; TE-300/TI-300 anode outlet temperature
recommendations: Add high feed flow alarm on FIT-100

deviation: Less Composition | Feed steam-to-carbon ratio
causes: Water pump failure/low water flow while NG flow continues (FIT-100 measures only total feed)
consequences: Carbon is deposited on the reformer catalyst and anode. This blocks gas channels, raises pressure drop, deactivates the catalyst and causes irreversible stack damage.
safeguards: FIT-100/FI-100 total feed flow
recommendations: Provide separate NG and water flow measurement with a low steam-to-carbon ratio alarm and trip of NG supply

deviation: Other than Composition | Feed (sulphur/contaminants in natural gas)
causes: Desulphurisation upstream fails or is saturated, or the NG supply is off-spec
consequences: Sulphur poisons the reformer catalyst and Ni anode, causing progressive voltage loss and stack degradation.
safeguards: VE-100/VZA-100 cell voltage monitoring
recommendations: Provide sulphur breakthrough monitoring/periodic analysis downstream of the desulphuriser

deviation: Other than Phase | Feed (liquid water carry-over)
causes: Upstream vaporiser/heat exchanger failure lets liquid water reach the stack inlet
consequences: Liquid water hits the 650 °C reformer, causing thermal shock, cracking of catalyst/plates and local quenching of cells.
safeguards: TE-100/TI-100 feed temperature
recommendations: Add low feed temperature alarm/trip on TE-100 to close LCV-100

deviation: Less Flow | H2 BOG to anode
causes: BOG compressor trip, low boil-off rate or LCV-300 fails closed
consequences: Fuel to the anode drops and fuel utilisation rises. Power output falls, the propulsion load cannot be met, and the anode is at risk of local fuel starvation.
safeguards: FIT-120/FI-120; PIT-120/PI-120; IIC-400 current control; VZA-100 low voltage alarm

deviation: More Flow | H2 BOG to anode
causes: LCV-300 fails open, IIC-400 fault, or BOG surge from the cargo tanks
consequences: Excess H2 oxidation without the matching endothermic reforming leads to stack overheating. Excess unburnt H2 goes to the anode outlet, creating a flammable atmosphere downstream.
recommendations: Provide high H2 BOG flow alarm and high-high stack temperature trip closing LCV-300 (independent of BPCS)

deviation: More Temperature | Stack (anode/cathode)
causes: BPCS temperature control failure, TE-200/TE-210 reading falsely low, loss of reforming heat sink, high current or low cathode air
consequences: Above about 700 °C the electrolyte evaporates and wet seals fail. Hot H2/CO can leak into the enclosure with fire/explosion risk and severe stack damage.
safeguards: TE-200/TI-200, TE-210/TI-210, TT-410; TE-300/TI-300, TE-310/TI-310; BPCS stack temperature control
recommendations: Implement SIL 1 high-high stack temperature trip (voted TE-200/TE-210) closing LCV-100/LCV-300 and reducing load; Provide TE deviation alarm between TE-200 and TE-210

deviation: Less Temperature | Stack (anode/cathode)
causes: Excess air or feed flow, prolonged low load/idle, or low inlet temperatures (TE-100/110/120)
consequences: Carbonate electrolyte solidifies and the matrix cracks, causing gas crossover between anode and cathode and permanent stack loss.
safeguards: TE-200/TE-210, TT-410; TE-100/TE-110/TE-120 inlet temperature indication
recommendations: Add low stack temperature alarm with automatic load/air adjustment and a hot-standby heating procedure

deviation: More Pressure | Stack (blocked outlet)
causes: BV-400 or BV-410 closes spuriously (fail-closed on signal/air loss) while inlet flows continue
consequences: Stack overpressure causes wet-seal blow-out, anode/cathode gas crossover and mixing of H2/CO with air at 650 °C. This can cause internal combustion, fire or explosion and release from the stack.
safeguards: PSV-160 to Vent Out; BV-160 vent valve (fail open); PIT-100/PIT-110/PIT-120 inlet pressure indication
recommendations: Interlock closure of BV-400/BV-410 to close LCV-100/LCV-200/LCV-300 and open BV-160; Add stack pressure transmitter with high-high pressure trip (SIL 2 assessment); Verify PSV-160 sizing for blocked-outlet case

deviation: Other than Pressure | Anode-cathode differential pressure
causes: Imbalance between air control (LCV-200) and fuel control (LCV-100/LCV-300), or sudden loss of air pressure
consequences: Wet seal/electrolyte matrix breakthrough lets fuel cross into the cathode (or air into the anode). This causes direct combustion, hot spots, stack fire and permanent damage.
safeguards: PIT-110, PIT-100, PIT-120 inlet pressure indication; BPCS pressure control
recommendations: Install anode-cathode differential pressure transmitter with alarm and trip

deviation: More Flow | Vent line (BV-160 / PSV-160)
causes: BV-160 opens spuriously (fail open on signal/air loss), or PSV-160 lifts/passes
consequences: Hot H2/CO-rich gas is released to Vent Out, forming a flammable/toxic cloud on deck with possible ignition, and stack pressure is lost.
safeguards: PSV-160 set pressure; Vent Out routed outside the skid
recommendations: Confirm vent outlet is located in a safe area per class rules, with dispersion study; Add position indication/alarm on BV-160

deviation: Reverse Flow | Anode Out / Cathode Out
causes: Stack pressure drops during shutdown/trip while the downstream header remains pressurised, or BV-400/BV-410 is passing
consequences: Air/exhaust enters the anode, oxidising the Ni anode. A flammable mixture may form inside the stack.
safeguards: BV-400 and BV-410 fail-closed valves
recommendations: Install non-return valves on anode and cathode outlets; Provide inert gas purge on shutdown

deviation: Reverse Flow | Air / Feed / H2 BOG inlets
causes: Loss of upstream compressor/supply pressure while the stack is still pressurised
consequences: Hot fuel gas flows back into the air line (or air into the fuel lines), forming a flammable mixture upstream with fire/explosion risk.
safeguards: PIT-110, PIT-100, PIT-120 pressure indication
recommendations: Install non-return valves upstream of LCV-100, LCV-200 and LCV-300; Low inlet pressure trip closing the respective LCV

deviation: Other than Flow | Stack external leak
causes: Wet seal degradation, corrosion, thermal cycling or ship motion/vibration
consequences: H2/CO released into the fuel cell room causes fire/explosion and toxic CO exposure to crew.
recommendations: Provide H2 and CO gas detection in the stack enclosure with ESD isolating LCV-100/LCV-300; Provide mechanical ventilation of the enclosure with monitoring per class rules

deviation: More Power | DC-Power output
causes: Propulsion overload demand, short circuit downstream, or IIC-400 current control fault
consequences: High current means high fuel utilisation, causing fuel starvation, cell reversal, local overheating and anode oxidation.
safeguards: IE-300/II-300/IR-300 current indication and recording; IT-400/IIC-400 current control; VE-100/VZA-100 low voltage alarm
recommendations: Provide overcurrent protection and load-limiting by power management system; Interlock current limit to available fuel flow (FIT-100/FIT-120)

deviation: No Power | DC-Power output
causes: Load disconnection/breaker trip, or stack trip
consequences: The vessel loses propulsion, with risk of collision/grounding. At open circuit the cell voltage is high, no reaction heat is produced, unreacted fuel goes to the anode outlet and the stack cools.
safeguards: VE-110/VZA-110 high voltage alarm; IIC-400 adjusting LCV-100/200/300; Multiple stack modules in plant
recommendations: Ensure power management reduces fuel automatically on load loss; Verify redundancy of propulsion power (other modules/battery) per class requirements

deviation: Reverse Power | DC-Power output
causes: Back-feed from battery/other parallel modules into a weak or tripped stack
consequences: Cells are driven in reverse (electrolysis), causing anode/cathode corrosion and stack damage.
safeguards: IE-300/II-300 current indication
recommendations: Provide blocking diode/reverse current protection on DC output

deviation: Other than Power | Cell voltage deviation
causes: Individual cell degradation, local fuel starvation or flow maldistribution
consequences: Weak cells reverse, causing local hot spots, electrolyte loss and possible seal failure leading to a gas leak.
safeguards: VE-100/VZA-100 low voltage alarm; VE-110/VZA-110 high voltage alarm; BPCS cell voltage deviation monitoring
recommendations: Provide automatic load reduction on high cell voltage deviation

deviation: Less Composition | CO2 at cathode
causes: High share of H2 BOG relative to natural gas feed (little CO2 in anode exhaust recycled to cathode)
consequences: Carbonate ions are not regenerated, so electrolyte is depleted, cell voltage drops and performance degrades.
safeguards: FIT-100 and FIT-120 flow indication; VZA-100 low voltage alarm
recommendations: Define minimum NG/BOG ratio in control philosophy, or CO2 make-up

deviation: Before Operation | Start-up fuel admission
causes: Fuel (LCV-100/LCV-300) admitted before the stack is purged and heated, due to operator error or sequence fault
consequences: Residual air and fuel form a flammable mixture inside the hot stack, leading to internal explosion and stack destruction.
safeguards: BPCS start-up control; TE-200/TE-210 temperature indication
recommendations: Implement start-up permissives (purge complete, stack temperature) on LCV-100/LCV-300; Provide inert gas purge system and written start-up procedure

deviation: No Utility | Instrument air / control power
causes: Loss of instrument air or control power to the valves
consequences: BV-400 and BV-410 close and BV-160 opens. If LCV-100/LCV-200/LCV-300 do not fail closed, fuel continues into the stack and is vented through Vent Out, giving a flammable release, possible overpressure and loss of propulsion.
safeguards: BV-160 fail-open vent; PSV-160
recommendations: Define and verify fail-closed position of LCV-100 and LCV-300 (fuel) and appropriate fail position of LCV-200; Provide UPS for BPCS and stack monitoring
